slides.1.title: 🔍 Italy’s Least-Known Wine Region
slides.1.content:
Molise is Italy’s second-smallest region. Lying south of Abruzzo, it was formerly part of Abruzzo and only became an independent region in 1963. It sits on the eastern side of the Southern Apennines, is mostly mountainous, and has only a short Adriatic coastline.

🔑 Key facts: the climate is Mediterranean on the coast and increasingly continental up into the mountains. Under Abruzzo’s influence, Montepulciano and Trebbiano lead, red grapes account for over 70%, and the native Tintilia is Molise’s signature.

slides.3.title: 🍇 Molise’s Grape Varieties
slides.3.content:
🍇 Abruzzo’s influence and the native Tintilia

Molise’s grapes are strongly influenced by Abruzzo: Montepulciano is the most planted variety and Trebbiano the most important white; red grapes account for over 70%. The native Tintilia covers a small area but is Molise’s signature. Other varieties include Aglianico, Sangiovese, Ciliegiolo, Falanghina, Greco, Malvasia Bianca, Moscato Bianco and Bombino Bianco.

🔴 Tintilia (red)

Status: considered native to Molise and the region’s signature grape

Origin: considered native but with no concrete evidence; some believe it came from Spain

Style: deep colour, full body, notable acidity, fine tannins

Today: traditionally blended with Montepulciano; still a minor variety, but enthusiasm is growing

🔴 Montepulciano (red)

Status: Molise’s most planted grape

Origin: from neighbouring Abruzzo

Role: the backbone of Molise DOC Rosso and Biferno Rosso

Partner: traditionally blended with Tintilia

⚪ Trebbiano (white)

Status: the most significant white grapes are Trebbiano Abruzzese and Trebbiano Toscano

Most planted: Trebbiano Abruzzese is Molise’s most planted white grape

Role: Biferno Bianco is based on Trebbiano Toscano

Other whites: Falanghina, Greco, Malvasia Bianca, Bombino Bianco
slides.4.title: 🏛️ Tintilia del Molise DOC
slides.4.content:
🏆 Tintilia del Molise DOC (2011) is Molise’s most important appellation, dedicated to promoting this distinctive native grape. Tintilia was traditionally only blended with Montepulciano and was largely forgotten; today more and more varietal bottlings are appearing, and it has become Molise’s calling card.

🍷 Rosso

The main style

Grape: Tintilia 95%+

Colour: deep

Flavours: black cherry, spice, violet

Style: full body, notable acidity, fine tannins

Riserva: min. 2 years’ ageing

🌸 Rosato

Fresh summer style

Grape: Tintilia 95%+

Maceration: short skin contact

Flavours: wild strawberry, white pepper, flowers

Style: fresh and fruity

Pairing: grilled seafood, summer salads
slides.5.title: 🍷 The DOCs of Molise
slides.5.content:
🌿 Molise DOC

Status: the regional DOC, largest in area and most productive

Scope: covers almost the whole of Molise

Rosso: based on Montepulciano

Varietals: many varietal wines, including international grapes (e.g. Cabernet Sauvignon)

Styles: red, rosé, white, sparkling, frizzante, Passito and more — the widest range

🍷 Biferno DOC (1983)

Scope: Campobasso province, named after the Biferno, Molise’s principal river

Red grapes: mainly Montepulciano, with Aglianico

White grapes: Trebbiano Toscano-based blends

Style: close to Abruzzo’s Montepulciano

🏔️ Pentro di Isernia DOC (1983)

Scope: the mountains of Isernia province (western Molise); also called Pentro

Name: from the Pentri, an ancient Samnite tribe

Red grapes: Montepulciano and Sangiovese

Key facts: very small production, mostly sold locally
slides.6.title: 🏺 Molise History and Culture
slides.6.content:
⏳ From mountain tribes to an independent region: Molise was the land of the ancient Samnites, and the name Pentro di Isernia comes from the Samnite Pentri tribe. Molise long shared an administrative region with Abruzzo and only became independent in 1963, so its grapes and training systems are strongly influenced by Abruzzo.

Antiquity

🏺 The Samnite tribes

The mountains of Molise were home to the Samnites, of whom the Pentri were one branch; they were later conquered by Rome.

Early modern

🇪🇸 The mystery of Tintilia’s origins

Molise was long part of the Kingdom of Naples, for a time under Spanish rule; some believe Tintilia was brought from Spain then, but there is no concrete evidence, and it is generally considered native to Molise.

Modern era

📅 Independence and the DOC system

1963: separated from Abruzzo / 1983: Biferno DOC and Pentro di Isernia DOC / later: the regional Molise DOC / 2011: Tintilia del Molise DOC
slides.7.title: 🍽️ Molise Food and Wine Pairing
slides.7.content:
🌾 Simple country cooking and wine

Molise’s cuisine is simple and traditional, built on handmade pasta, lamb and seafood, combining the best of the mountains and the coast.

🍝 Cavatelli

  • Shell-shaped handmade pasta
  • With lamb ragù (Ragù d'Agnello)
  • ✅ Tintilia del Molise Rosso
  • ✅ Biferno Rosso

🐟 Brodetto alla Termolese

  • Termoli-style fish soup
  • Several fish, tomato, chilli
  • ✅ Molise Falanghina
  • ✅ Biferno Bianco

🧀 Caciocavallo Molisano

  • Molise’s traditional stretched-curd cheese
  • Semi-hard cow’s-milk cheese
  • ✅ Tintilia Riserva (aged cheese)
  • ✅ Molise Greco (fresh cheese)

🍖 Agnello alla Brace

  • Seasoned with herbs, rosemary and garlic
  • A traditional mountain dish of Molise
  • ✅ Tintilia del Molise Riserva
  • ✅ Pentro Rosso
slides.8.title: ❓ Why Is Molise So Little Known?
slides.8.content:
🔍 A hidden gem: Molise has a distinctive native grape and long traditions, yet for many reasons it has long been overlooked — which is exactly what makes it such a rewarding region to explore.

⚠️ Why it is little known (6 reasons)

  • Small size: Italy’s second-smallest region
  • Short history: independent from Abruzzo only in 1963
  • No DOCG: no top quality label
  • Depopulation: young people leave, vineyards age
  • Bulk-wine tradition: wine was mostly sold in bulk
  • Location: surrounded by bigger regions (Abruzzo, Campania)

💎 The hidden-gem opportunity

  • Great value: distinctive grapes at friendly prices
  • A rare experience: Tintilia is a rare Italian grape
  • Tintilia DOC: its own appellation since 2011
  • Quality on the rise: more and more quality-focused small producers
  • Varietal wines: Molise DOC allows many varietal wines
  • Leading estate: Di Majo Norante is Molise’s best-known winery
slides.9.title: 📜 Molise Appellations in Full (IWS Course Material)
slides.9.content:
🌿 Tintilia del Molise DOC (2011)

A recent DOC dedicated to Tintilia: min. 95% Tintilia; Riserva min. 2 years’ ageing. For a varietal Tintilia, this is the DOC to look for.

🍷 Molise DOC

The regional DOC, covering almost the whole of Molise, the largest and most productive. A wide range of styles: a Montepulciano-based Rosso and many varietal wines (including international grapes). A varietal Cabernet Sauvignon is most likely to come from this DOC. Note: Molise DOC is not red-only and does allow varietal wines.

🏞️ Biferno DOC

Named after the Biferno, Molise’s principal river. Reds are based on Montepulciano; a Trebbiano Toscano-based white blend is most likely to come from this DOC.

🏔️ Pentro di Isernia / Pentro DOC and IGT

Pentro di Isernia (also called Pentro) lies in the mountains of Isernia province in the west. The regional IGT is Terre degli Osci. Molise has no DOCG.

slides.10.title: 🧬 Tintilia in Depth
slides.10.content:
🧬 Tintilia: Molise’s signature grape

Origin

  • Native? considered native to Molise, but with no concrete evidence
  • The Spanish theory: some believe it was brought from Spain
  • Name: often linked to the Spanish word tinto (red)
  • Traditional use: blended with Montepulciano

Characteristics

  • Colour: deep
  • Body: full
  • Acidity: notable
  • Tannins: fine
  • Today: a minor variety, but enthusiasm is growing

🍷 Tintilia styles by level

Standard Tintilia

Black cherry, violet, spice

Fruit-led, fine tannins

Drink: now–5 years

Tintilia Riserva

Min. 2 years’ ageing

More structure and more layers

Drink: 3–10 years

Tintilia Rosato

Red berries, flowers

Fresh and fruity

Drink: 1–3 years

Tintilia’s appeal: deep and full-bodied, yet with notable acidity and fine tannins — an expression of the character of Molise’s mountain terroir.
slides.11.title: 🏞️ Topography, Climate and Soils (IWS Course Material)
slides.11.content:
🏞️ A mostly mountainous region: Molise lies on the eastern side of the Southern Apennines, is mostly mountainous, and has only a short Adriatic coastline. Its principal river, the Biferno, flows east into the Adriatic, while the Volturno in the west flows towards Campania.

☀️ Climate

🌊 Coast

Mediterranean climate

🏔️ Mountains

Increasingly continental further into the mountains

🏙️ Two provinces

Campobasso (east, reaching the coast) and Isernia (western mountains)

🌿 Training

The traditional Pergola Abruzzese trellis; new vineyards mostly use cordone speronato

🪨 Soils

Coastal areas

Sand and clay

Inland areas

Limestone and marl

The Biferno valley

Biferno DOC is named after this river, in Campobasso province

The Isernia mountains

The western uplands, home of Pentro di Isernia DOC
slides.12.title: 🔄 Traditional and Modern Winemaking
slides.12.content:
📈 From bulk wine to bottled wine: Molise used to produce mostly bulk wine, and Tintilia was usually blended with Montepulciano. Since Tintilia del Molise DOC was created in 2011, more and more estates bottle it as a varietal, showing Molise’s own character.

⚠️ Traditional approach

  • Training: Pergola Abruzzese trellis, high yields
  • Grapes: mainly Montepulciano and Trebbiano
  • Tintilia: blended with Montepulciano
  • Sales: mostly bulk wine

🚀 Modern direction

  • Training: cordone speronato in rows
  • Grapes: varietal Tintilia, plus varietal wines under Molise DOC
  • Levels: Tintilia Riserva aged at least 2 years
  • Sales: small quality estates competing internationally with bottled wine

📅 The Tintilia revival

slides.13.title: 🍾 The Many Styles of Molise DOC
slides.13.content:
🍾 One DOC, many styles

Wine types

  • Rosso: based on Montepulciano
  • Rosato: rosé
  • Bianco: white
  • Spumante / Frizzante: sparkling / semi-sparkling
  • Passito: sweet wine from dried grapes
  • Riserva: the aged category

Varietal wines you may see

  • Red: Montepulciano, Aglianico, Tintilia, Sangiovese
  • White: Falanghina, Greco, Trebbiano, Moscato Bianco
  • International: e.g. Cabernet Sauvignon
  • Rules: the exact grapes and percentages are set by the disciplinare (production rules)

🌸 How to choose

IWS exam points: Molise DOC is the regional and most productive DOC, allows varietal wines and is not red-only; Molise Rosso is based on Montepulciano.
slides.14.title: 🏰 Leading Molise Producers
slides.14.content:
🏰 Leading Molise producers

Most Molise wineries are small family estates; the following represent the different styles of Molise wine.

🥇 Di Majo Norante (Campomarino)

Standing: Molise’s best-known winery

Location: Campomarino, near the Adriatic coast

Flagship: Don Luigi Riserva, Montepulciano-based

Hallmarks: also makes Tintilia and many Molise varietal wines

🌿 Borgo di Colloredo (Campomarino)

Standing: a family estate in the coastal area

Wines: Tintilia, Biferno and more

Hallmarks: tradition alongside modernity

🎨 Claudio Cipressi (San Felice del Molise)

Standing: a Tintilia specialist

Flagship: Macchiarossa Tintilia del Molise

Hallmarks: focused on the pure character of Tintilia

💰 Cantine Salvatore (Ururi)

Standing: a quality estate in Campobasso province

Wines: Tintilia del Molise

Hallmarks: a good way into Molise

⭐ Campi Valerio (Monteroduni)

Standing: an estate in Isernia province

Wines: Tintilia del Molise

Hallmarks: in the western mountains, the Pentro di Isernia area
